Olinda lies near Recife in northeastern Brazil. The city was founded in 1535, and its historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Dense historic neighborhoods spread across its hills, with churches, monasteries and small squares.

Baroque religious buildings, colorful facades and red tiled roofs stand out in the cityscape. The historic center is easy to explore on foot, gradually climbing to higher points and open viewpoints.

Olinda is also famous for its carnival. On an Ada Tours itinerary, it pairs naturally with Recife before the journey continues to Pernambuco's beach destinations.

Ollagüe stands on the border between Bolivia and Chile and forms part of the mountain scenery of the Altiplano. Its massif rises above dry, open terrain. On Bolivian itineraries, the volcano is viewed alongside high-altitude lagoons and the Chiguana Salt Flat.

The surrounding area reveals volcanic slopes alongside broad plains. The shapes of the mountains, rocky ground and distant panoramas are especially striking here. Ollagüe adds a natural highlight to a journey through southwestern Bolivia: the highland terrain is clearly visible, and the massif serves as a landmark on the route between different parts of the Altiplano.

Ollantaytambo lies in the Sacred Valley of the Incas and preserves traces of ancient town planning. Its streets and water channels reflect Inca heritage, while the stone terraces of the archaeological complex rise above the residential area. The historic landscape extends beyond the monument itself into the town.

The complex served religious, agricultural and military purposes. Visitors can examine its enormous stone masonry, terraces and the positioning of structures on the hillside. Ollantaytambo offers an insight into the layout of an Inca settlement surrounded by mountains and enriches a journey between Cusco, the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu.

Orange Walk is one of Belize's six districts, with a population of just over forty thousand. Affectionately nicknamed "Sugar City," the district is also known for cattle farming and rum production.

Greenery is everywhere, along with numerous attractions and reminders of the Maya ruins.

Excursions take visitors to the famous Maya ruins of Lamanai and Cuello. The jungles of Orange Walk are home to more than 400 bird species, more than anywhere else in the country, making the area a paradise for birdwatchers.

If you wish to continue farther north after enjoying Orange Walk, the border town of Corozal is 30 miles away, along with a free zone for shopping enthusiasts.

An excursion to Orongo introduces the Tangata Manu, or Birdman, tradition. The program describes stone houses where clans awaited the arrival of the manutara bird and a competition for the right to choose the chief. A visit to the village is combined with a view of the Rano Kau crater.
